title: Embedded Onboarding Playbook for Product and Platform Teams
author: Anika Rao
body:
Overview:

Purpose
This playbook defines a repeatable, lightweight embedded onboarding pattern tailored for hires joining Product and Platform teams at Redwood. It aligns role ramp expectations, tooling access timelines, manager and mentor responsibilities, and a standardized handover template so new joiners reach measurable impact faster while minimizing operational friction.

Scope
- Applies to full-time ICs (levels IC1–IC5) and engineering managers joining Product, Platform, and Core infra teams.
- Not a replacement for team-specific PRDs or technical deep dives; it supplements those with operational and people processes.

Owners and Escalation
- Playbook owner: People Ops (Anika Rao).
- Tier 1 operational owner for tooling: Platform Operations (SRE) team.
- Escalation: raise to People Ops if provisioning SLAs exceed thresholds (see Access SLA section).

Principles
1) Predictable first 30 days: reduce variability across teams with a 0–30 day milestone map.
2) Role-tailored but consistent: core checkpoints are uniform; technical ramp content varies by team.
3) Manager-driven outcomes, mentor-supported development: managers set goals; mentors help reduce cognitive overhead.
4) Automated, auditable provisioning: avoid ad-hoc access requests.

Quick Start (for hiring manager)
1. Fill the Embedded Onboarding Form (People Ops template) at offer acceptance.
2. Assign a primary mentor and a technical buddy before Day 0.
3. Confirm required tool access and sensitive systems with Platform Ops within 48 hours.
4. Publish the 90-day success criteria in the team’s workspace.

Preboarding Checklist (to complete before Day 0)
- Offer paperwork processed and payroll setup confirmed.
- Laptop chosen and procurement ticket created (include required GPU/VM specs if applicable).
- Identity (SSO) account created with base groups: contributor, slack, okta.
- Read-ahead packet sent (team charter, current roadmap, recent design reviews).
- First-week calendar blocks created: 1:1s, team orientation, mentor syncs.

Day 0–1: Immediate Priorities
- 1:1 with manager (goal-setting and success criteria).
- Intro to mentor and buddy: schedule recurring check-ins (2x/week first month).
- Verify basic access (email, Slack, docs, code repo read).
- Run start script: redwood-setup onboard --confirm (see Examples).

Week 1–2: Build Context and Triage Access
- Complete team architecture walkthrough and architecture docs.
- Shadow a deployment/release and an on-call rotation (platform hires).
- Confirm additional service-specific access (service accounts, deploy keys).
- Deliverable: short note in team channel summarizing understanding and questions.

Weeks 3–8: First Scoped Deliverable
- Owner and manager agree a scoped ticket that can land in 2–4 weeks.
- Weekly progress updates in the team’s sprint channel.
- Mentor assists with PR/CR reviews to speed feedback loop.

90-Day Outcomes (expected)
- New hire has delivered at least one scoped change and conducted a knowledge share.
- Manager has documented performance and learning plan for next 90 days.
- People Ops closes onboarding loop and records completion.

Role-Specific Orientation (high level)
- Product Engineers: focus first week on product metrics, user flows, A/B test signals, and feature flags.
- Platform Engineers: focus first week on CI/CD pipelines, infra dashboards, incident runbooks, and capacity controls.
- Product Managers joining engineering teams: ramp on metrics, release cadence, and Git workflow for PRs and specs.

Manager Responsibilities (checklist)
- Provide 90-day success criteria in writing by Day 1.
- Allocate a mentor and schedule recurring check-ins.
- Create a scoped deliverable and acceptance criteria by the end of Week 2.
- Ensure access requests are filed within first 48 hours and follow up to meet SLAs.

Mentor/Buddy Responsibilities
- First two weeks: daily ad-hoc availability and twice-weekly structured syncs.
- Review first three PRs within 48 hours.
- Facilitate introductions to core collaborators.

Tools & Access Matrix (example)
| System | Base Access (Day 0–1) | Role-Specific Access | Owner | SLA |
|--------|-----------------------|----------------------|-------|-----|
| Slack | Member | N/A | People Ops | 0–1 day |
| Confluence/docs | Read | Write (after training) | People Ops | 0–1 day |
| Git (repos) | Read on team repos | Write on assigned repos | Eng DevEx | 0–2 days |
| CI/CD (deploy) | No | Approve/Deploy for platform | Platform Ops | 2–7 days |
| Cloud console (prod) | No | IAM role-based access | Cloud Infra | 2–10 days |
| Monitoring/Dashboards | View | Alerting edit after training | SRE | 1–5 days |

Access SLA and Request Process
- Standard SLA targets:
  - Base access (email, Slack, docs): 24 hours.
  - Repository write and monitoring view: 48–72 hours.
  - Production console or service accounts: up to 10 business days (require approval).
- To request access: file ticket in Platform Ops queue with template: subject "Access request: <name> — <system>" and include manager approval.
- Escalation path: after SLA misses of 48 hours for base access, People Ops will intervene.

Handover and Knowledge Transfer Standards
- All handovers must include: short context paragraph, why change matters, architectural pointers, test coverage notes, and rollback steps.
- Use the team’s Handover Template (copyable from People Ops) and include at least one short demo recording (5–10 minutes).

Handover Template (pasteable)
1. Title and owner
2. Brief description and business impact
3. Key services and repos
4. Runbook excerpt and common failure modes
5. How to validate a successful change
6. Contacts and escalation path

Examples and CLI snippets
- Example: quick local setup (developer machine):
  1) git clone git@github.com:redwood/<team-repo>.git
  2) ./scripts/setup-dev.sh --minimal
  3) export REDWOOD_ENV=dev && ./bin/start-local
- Example: access bootstrap (internal CLI):
  $ redwood-iam request --user anika@redwood.com --role repo-write --reason "onboarding product team"
  # check status
  $ redwood-iam status --request-id RQ-12345

Measurement and Feedback
- People Ops will run a 30-day survey to measure ramp clarity, tool access friction, and mentor effectiveness.
- Key metrics: time-to-first-merge, time-to-deploy, Days-to-base-access (median).
- Quarterly retro: managers and mentors meet to refine the embedded onboarding checklist.

Common Pitfalls and Mitigations
- Pitfall: missing service accounts delaying development. Mitigation: copy standard service-account request during preboarding.
- Pitfall: overloaded mentors. Mitigation: cap active mentees to 2 per mentor and use rotation windows.

Appendix A — Template: 90-Day Success Criteria (example)
- Objective: Complete a cross-team bug fix that traverses frontend, backend, and infra validation and ship with documentation.
- Success metrics: PR merged, automated tests green, deployment to staging, and a short knowledge share recorded.

Appendix B — Suggested Onboarding Reading List
- Team README and architecture map
- Last three release notes and postmortems
- API contracts and SLOs for services you will own

Frequently Asked Questions
Q: Who signs off when accesses are delayed?
A: The hiring manager and People Ops. For production-level access, Cloud Infra approval is required.

Q: Can a mentor be from a different team?
A: Yes — cross-team mentors are encouraged if they reduce context-switching and are familiar with the core tech stack.

Related resources

- Platform Ops: access request flow and SLAs
- Team workspace: add the new hire to the team’s onboarding page
